Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself to break down a complex problem into smaller, manageable pieces. You can think of it like Russian nesting dolls, where you keep opening each doll until you reach the solid one at the very center. In programming, this final solid doll is called the base case, which tells the function when to stop calling itself and prevents an infinite loop. Once the base case is reached, the function passes the results back up the chain to solve the original task.
